# Multi-Page Accessibility Audit & Testing Plan

> **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after audit execution.
> **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA
> **Users who need accessibility:** All users; screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver); keyboard-only users; low-vision users (magnification, high-contrast); mobile users (iOS VO, TalkBack); voice-input users (Dragon)
> **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), TalkBack (Android), keyboard-only navigation, Dragon NaturallySpeaking
> **Risk Level:** High (legacy 20-page site, high-stakes government portal, VPAT deadline, third-party components, unknown baseline accessibility state)
> **Audit Type:** Pre-VPAT systematic conformance evaluation
> **Timeline:** 3 months, 2-person QA team

**Feature:** Comprehensive pre-VPAT accessibility audit and conformance testing for a 20-page government benefits portal
**Component Type:** Multi-page site audit (platform: server-rendered HTML + progressive JS enhancement)
**Scope:** Public pages (7), authenticated flows (6), shared patterns (8), third-party integrations (3)

---

## Scope & Context

### What
Pre-VPAT accessibility audit of an existing 20-page government benefits portal (4 years old, incremental fixes but no systematic audit) to establish WCAG 2.2 AA baseline, identify remediation scope, and produce ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 publication document within 3 months.

### Why
The portal serves citizens applying for public assistance—critical access for a vulnerable population. VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) is required for government procurement compliance; inaccessibility blocks applicants with disabilities from self-serve benefits navigation.

### Who Needs Accessibility
- Screen reader users: NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), iOS VoiceOver, TalkBack (Android)
- Keyboard-only users: No mouse available, rely on Tab, Enter, arrow keys, Escape
- Low-vision users: Screen magnification (up to 400% zoom per WCAG 1.4.10), high-contrast mode, adjustable text size
- Cognitive users: Clear error messages, consistent navigation, no surprises
- Deaf users: Captions on embedded YouTube videos
- Voice-control users: Dragon NaturallySpeaking, iOS Voice Control, Android Voice Access

### Compliance Target
WCAG 2.2 AA (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines Level AA) per Section 508 and government procurement standards. Success: all 50 Level A and Level AA criteria met across all tested pages.

### Assistive Technologies
**Desktop screen readers:**
- NVDA (Windows): Browse mode, Forms mode, landmark navigation
- JAWS (Windows): virtual PC cursor mode, Forms mode, heading/landmark hotkeys
- VoiceOver (macOS): rotor navigation, trackpad gestures, focus management

**Mobile screen readers:**
- iOS VoiceOver: single-finger gestures, rotor for landmarks/headings/links
- TalkBack (Android): local context menu, reading/navigation mode

**Navigation methods:**
- Keyboard: Tab (next), Shift+Tab (prev), Enter/Space (activate), arrow keys (composite widgets), Escape (close), roving tabindex (tabs, menus, trees)

**Vision aids:**
- Screen magnification: 200%, 400% zoom without horizontal scroll (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow)
- High-contrast mode: Windows High Contrast, forced colors CSS
- Text sizing: rem/em-based, user zoom, adjustable line-height

**Input alternatives:**
- Dragon NaturallySpeaking: speak form labels, button names, link text to navigate and activate
- Sticky keys: chord-based keyboard shortcuts without simultaneous key press

### Regulatory & Timeline Context
- **ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508:** Template structure requires criterion-by-criterion conformance claims (Y/N/N/A)
- **Deadline:** 3 months (12 weeks)
- **Team:** 2 QA engineers (no accessibility specialists on staff initially)
- **Tools:** axe DevTools Enterprise (licensed), Playwright (open-source)
- **Constraints:** Cannot defer third-party components (reCAPTCHA, YouTube); must document known-third-party exceptions per VPAT standards

---

## Page Sampling Strategy

**Foundation:** W3C Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 1.0 and 2.0 concepts — not all 20 pages require equal test depth. Risk-based sampling focuses on:
- High-risk pages (authenticated flows, form submission)
- Shared component patterns (navigation, search, alerts)
- Page type representatives (home, detail, dashboard, error states)

### Page Grouping & Sampling Rationale

**Group A: Public Landing Pages (Risk: Low-Medium)**
- Home, About, FAQ, News, Contact
- **Sampling:** Test Home + Contact (2 of 5) — Home represents site entry point, Contact tests form + reCAPTCHA
- **Rationale:** Public pages have lower complexity; fixing shared nav/search benefits all

**Group B: Content Pages (Risk: Low)**
- Program Listings, Program Detail (×3 variants)
- **Sampling:** Test Listings + Detail variant 1 (2 of 4) — variants share same structure
- **Rationale:** Content-heavy; key audit: heading hierarchy, link quality, embedded video captions

**Group C: Authenticated Flows (Risk: High)**
- Account creation, Login, Multi-step form (6 steps), Document upload, Status dashboard, Notifications
- **Sampling:** Test ALL (6 of 6) — auth flows control access; any barrier blocks users; form validation, focus management critical
- **Rationale:** Highest risk; small sample set (6 pages)

**Group D: Shared Components (Test once, verify across all pages)**
- Global navigation (mega-menu), search (live results), alerts/notifications, data tables, file upload, date picker, session timeout modal, reCAPTCHA v2
- **Sampling:** Extract components and test in isolation FIRST, then verify in context on sample pages
- **Rationale:** One fixed nav benefits all 20 pages; efficient leverage

**Group E: Third-Party Integrations (Risk: Cannot Remediate)**
- reCAPTCHA v2 (login, contact forms)
- YouTube embedded videos (program pages)
- Analytics script (no WCAG implications)
- **Sampling:** Test for context & label quality; document third-party inaccessibility in VPAT Appendix C
- **Rationale:** Cannot fix third-party code; VPAT requires documentation

### Execution Order
1. **Week 1-2:** Automated scan (axe-core) on all 20 pages for quick baseline (known issues, duplicate findings)
2. **Week 2-3:** Manual audit Group C (authenticated, highest risk) + Group D (shared components)
3. **Week 3-4:** Manual audit Group B (content pages) + Group A (landing pages)
4. **Week 4-5:** Screen reader testing (priority pages)
5. **Week 5-6:** Visual regression (contrast, zoom, high-contrast mode)
6. **Week 6-8:** Remediation & regression testing
7. **Week 8-12:** VPAT compilation, legal review, final audit

**Total sample coverage:** 12 pages out of 20 tested manually (60%), 20 pages automated scan, 100% indirect coverage via shared components

---

## Tool Selection & Rationale

### Automated Testing: axe DevTools Enterprise
**What:** Rule-based WCAG 2.2 AA engine; browser DevTools integration
**Strengths:** Catches contrast, alt text, ARIA misuse, form labeling, heading hierarchy, landmark duplication
**Blindspots:** Focus management, live-region announcements, keyboard trap cycles, screen reader interaction order, APG pattern completeness
**Configuration:**
```
- Standard WCAG 2.2 AA ruleset enabled
- axe DevTools Enterprise: enable "Experimental rules" = OFF (focus on stable findings)
- Scanning mode: Scan full page (not isolated components)
- Exclude: reCAPTCHA iframe, YouTube embed iframe, Google Analytics script
- Report format: JSON export for VPAT criteria mapping
```
**Use on:** All 20 pages (batch scan), then every page after remediation to prevent regression

### Manual Keyboard Testing: Playwright + Custom Harness
**What:** Scripted keyboard navigation verification (no synthetic events; real CDP `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`)
**Test matrix:**
```
Tab order: Tab key cycles through all interactive elements; order matches visual left-to-right, top-to-bottom
Button/link activation: Enter/Space activates buttons; Enter activates links
Escape key: Closes dialogs/modals/menus
Arrow keys: Navigate within composite widgets (tabs, menu, listbox, date picker)
Focus trap: Tab within modal cycles between first/last focusable element
Focus restoration: After modal/menu close, focus returns to trigger element
Focus indicator visibility: Outline visible at 200% zoom, 400% zoom, high-contrast mode
Skip link: First focusable element is "Skip to main content" link
Form navigation: Tab moves between form fields; Shift+Tab reverses
Session timeout warning: Modal appears, focus moves to it, Escape closes and restores focus
```
**Use on:** Group C (authenticated), Group D (shared components), Group B (content)

### Screen Reader Testing: Real Assistive Tech + Codified Checks
**Matrix: Which SR covers which page type**
| Page Type | NVDA (Win) | JAWS (Win) | VoiceOver (Mac) | iOS VO | TalkBack | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|--------|----------|-------|
| Home | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Entry point; high traffic |
| Contact form | ✓ | ✓ |  |  |  | Form interaction; desktop primary |
| Login | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |  | Critical; auth required; test form state |
| Multi-step form | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |  | 6 steps; progress indication; focus management |
| Status dashboard | ✓ |  | ✓ |  | ✓ | Data table; live updates; mixed SR coverage |
| Program detail | ✓ |  |  | ✓ |  | Video embed; content structure |

**Specific checks:**
- Page structure: landmarks announced (nav, main, aside, footer) in proper order per `<header>`/`<nav>`/`<main>`/`<footer>` HTML
- Heading hierarchy: h1 present, h2-h6 no skips, multiple h1s acceptable if section-scoped
- Link text: descriptive (not "click here"), new-window links marked "(opens in new window)"
- Form labels: associated via `<label for="">`, `aria-labelledby`, or `aria-label`; labels announced on focus
- Form errors: error message announced, associated with field via `aria-describedby`, field marked `aria-invalid="true"`
- Tables: `<table>`, `<th>` with scope, row headers for identifying cells, column headers announced
- Live regions: status updates announced (aria-live="polite"), alerts announced (aria-live="assertive" or role="alert")
- Dynamic content: new items announced; focus moves appropriately; user not disoriented

**Use on:** Group C, Group B sample, Group D sample pages

### Visual Regression Testing: Playwright Screenshots + Contrast Analysis
**What:** Automated screenshot capture + manual contrast verification at multiple zoom levels
**Test points:**
```
Contrast: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold), per WCAG 1.4.3
Focus indicators: visible, 2-color (outline + box-shadow), not lost at 200% zoom or high-contrast mode
Color + non-color: red error border + error icon + error text (not color alone)
200% zoom: layout reflows without horizontal scroll; all content readable
400% zoom: horizontal scroll acceptable per WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (only at 320px equivalent viewport)
High-contrast mode (Windows): colors applied via CSS custom properties or CSS forced-colors safe
prefers-reduced-motion: animations disabled for users with this preference (test `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`)
```
**Use on:** All sample pages (Group C, B, A, D)

---

## Testing Matrix & Execution Phases

| Phase | Scope | Tool(s) | Pages | Duration | Output | Owner |
|-------|-------|---------|-------|----------|--------|-------|
| 1. Baseline Scan | All 20 pages | axe DevTools | 20 | 1 week | Automated findings JSON, WCAG criterion map | QA 1 |
| 2. Component Audit | Shared patterns | Manual + WAVE | 8 components | 1 week | Finding list, APG pattern verification, structure stubs | QA 2 |
| 3. Auth Flow Audit | Login, signup, forms | Keyboard + SR | 6 pages | 1 week | Keyboard trap log, SR interaction notes, focus management audit | QA 1 + QA 2 |
| 4. Content Audit | Programs, detail | Manual + contrast | 4 pages | 1 week | Alt text audit, heading hierarchy, link text quality, video captions | QA 2 |
| 5. Landing Page Audit | Home, contact | Form + reCAPTCHA | 2 pages | 3 days | Form validation, 3P component handling notes | QA 1 |
| 6. Visual Audit | Sample pages | Screenshots + tools | 8 pages | 1 week | Contrast report, zoom screenshots, focus indicator verification | QA 1 |
| 7. Remediation | Code fixes | Playwright tests | TBD | 2 weeks | Fixed components, regression tests | Dev team |
| 8. VPAT Compilation | Criterion mapping | Manual review + axe | All 20 | 1 week | VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 document, Appendix C (third-party) | QA 1 |

**Total: 8-10 weeks, 2 QA engineers, 1 dev team for remediation**

---

## Prioritization Framework

Issues ranked by impact on user completion of critical tasks (applying for benefits, checking application status) rather than WCAG criterion severity alone.

### CRITICAL (Blocks Access)
User cannot complete a required task due to the defect.
- **Examples:** Login form has no associated labels (keyboard user cannot identify fields); modal has no Escape key handling (keyboard user cannot close); form submission fails with no error message (screen reader user unaware of error)
- **WCAG map:** 1.3.1 (Info & Relationships), 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 3.3.1 (Error Identification), 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value)
- **Action:** Fix immediately; re-test before proceeding

### MAJOR (Significant Friction)
Task completion is possible but significantly harder; workarounds exist.
- **Examples:** Focus restoration missing after modal close (user must Tab many times to re-orient); heading hierarchy skips h2-h3 (screen reader user cannot predict document structure, but can still read); image missing alt text (context clues substitute)
- **WCAG map:** 1.1.1 (Alt Text), 1.3.1 (Semantic structure), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), 4.1.3 (Status Messages)
- **Action:** Remediate in priority batches; test weekly

### MINOR (Inconvenience)
Accessibility could be better; does not significantly block task.
- **Examples:** Button has green background only (no icon/text), no high-contrast safe color pairs; link text is "read more" (unclear destination but context available)
- **WCAG map:** 1.4.1 (Use of Color), 2.4.4 (Link Purpose)
- **Action:** Include in sweeping fixes; lower priority if resource-constrained

### ADVISORY (Best Practice)
Not a WCAG violation, but accessibility best practice.
- **Examples:** Larger touch targets (44x44 instead of 40x40); live-region aria-live="polite" should be aria-live="assertive" for errors
- **WCAG map:** Emerging guidance, not WCAG 2.2 AA
- **Action:** Log for roadmap; deprioritize for 3-month VPAT deadline

---

## Handling Third-Party Components

### reCAPTCHA v2
**Status:** Not remedial (third-party, no source access)
**Known issues:** Confusing focus management, unclear instructions for keyboard users, poor screen reader support
**VPAT approach:**
- Test interaction: Can keyboard user Tab to/from reCAPTCHA? Can they complete the challenge without mouse?
- Document in VPAT Appendix C: "reCAPTCHA v2 provided by Google Inc. is a third-party component. Known accessibility limitations: [list specific defects]. Remediation: Google reCAPTCHA v3 (recommended) or reCAPTCHA Enterprise may offer improved accessibility. Current instance documented for transparency; remediation awaits vendor improvement."
- Do NOT claim conformance on reCAPTCHA itself; claim remediation plan in VPAT notes
- Consider upgrade path: reCAPTCHA v3 (no user interaction required) or third-party alternative (hCaptcha, etc.)

### YouTube Embedded Videos
**Status:** Not remedial (third-party content)
**Test:** Are videos captioned? Is player keyboard-accessible?
**VPAT approach:**
- For embedded videos, test iframe title and caption availability
- Document: "Embedded YouTube videos provided by Google. Accessibility depends on caption/transcript availability in source video. Organization responsible for sourcing captioned content; vendor player is keyboard-accessible."
- Requirement: All program videos MUST have captions or transcripts before VPAT publication
- Link to CC license requirement: Federal contractors must caption video per Section 508

### Google Analytics Script
**Status:** No WCAG implications (no visual/interactive content)
**Test:** None required
**VPAT approach:** Footnote in Appendix C (no accessibility relevance)

---

## Shared Component Leverage

Fixing once = benefits all 20 pages automatically. Prioritize:

**Component 1: Global Navigation (Mega-Menu)**
Appears on all 20 pages. Fix once: Tab order, Escape key, aria-expanded on toggle, all links descriptive, skip link presence → all pages automatically pass nav audit.
- **Files to audit:** Navigation template/component
- **APG pattern:** Menu Button (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubutton/)
- **Tests:** Tab into menu button, Space/Enter expands, arrow keys navigate, Escape closes, focus restores

**Component 2: Search with Live Results**
Appears on Home, Program Listings, Status Dashboard. Fix once: input labeled, results announced via aria-live, aria-busy during loading.
- **APG pattern:** Combobox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)
- **Tests:** Type in search, results appear with aria-live="polite", loading state via aria-busy="true"

**Component 3: Alert/Notification Inline Messages**
Appears on forms (validation errors), dashboards (application status), session timeout modal. Fix once: role="alert" or aria-live="assertive", aria-describedby link to input, aria-invalid="true" on invalid field.
- **Tests:** Error announced automatically, not just visual red border

**Component 4: Data Table (Application History)**
Appears on Status Dashboard. Fix once: `<table>`, `<th scope="col">` or `scope="row"`, headers announced.
- **WCAG:** 1.3.1 (table headers), 4.1.2 (scope attribute)
- **Tests:** Screen reader announces column/row headers

**Component 5: File Upload**
Appears on Document Upload page. Fix once: input labeled, file-type instructions via aria-describedby, validation errors linked.
- **Tests:** Label announced, file requirements clear, errors associated

**Component 6: Date Picker**
Appears in multi-step application form. Fix once: aria-expanded, arrow keys navigate dates, Enter selects, Escape closes.
- **APG pattern:** Date Picker (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/datepicker/)
- **Tests:** Keyboard navigation, focus management

**Component 7: Session Timeout Modal**
Appears on authenticated pages. Fix once: focus trap (Tab cycles within modal), Escape closes (with confirm), focus restores to trigger page.
- **APG pattern:** Modal Dialog (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialogmodal/)
- **Tests:** Tab/Shift+Tab stays in modal, Escape closes, focus returns

**Component 8: Form Validation Summary**
Appears on multi-step form. Fix once: role="alert" or aria-live="assertive", error summary lists links to invalid fields.
- **Tests:** Errors announced on submit, links jump to fields

---

## VPAT Reporting Structure

VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 requires criterion-by-criterion claims:
- **Conformant (Y):** Criterion met across all tested pages
- **Not Conformant (N):** Criterion not met; document specific failures
- **Not Applicable (N/A):** Feature not present in product

### Expected CRITICAL Findings (Common on Legacy Government Sites)
Based on typical 20-page legacy audits, expect high failure rates on:
- **2.4.3 Focus Order:** Tab order incorrect; focus doesn't restore after modal; roving tabindex not implemented in composite widgets
- **3.3.1 Error Identification:** Errors indicated only by color (red border) without text message or aria-invalid
- **1.1.1 Non-text Content:** Missing alt text on images; CSS pseudo-element icons not marked aria-hidden
- **1.3.1 Info & Relationships:** Form fields not labeled; table headers missing scope; landmark landmarks missing
- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value:** ARIA attributes missing or incorrect; buttons/toggles lack accessible names

### VPAT Appendix C (Explanatory Notes)
Document:
1. Audit methodology (WCAG-EM reference, pages tested, sample rationale)
2. Third-party components (reCAPTCHA, YouTube) with known issues
3. Conformance claims per criterion
4. Remediation plan (which issues will be fixed, timeline)

### Conformance Statement Template
```
[Portal Name] is designed to be accessible to users with disabilities. This Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) documents conformance to WCAG 2.2 Level AA (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines). The evaluation was conducted per the W3C Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM). [Portal] meets all WCAG 2.2 Level AA criteria except [list unmet criteria]. Remediation for identified gaps is planned for [date]. See Appendix C for methodology and third-party component notes.
```

---

## Testing Strategy & Acceptance Criteria

### Automated Testing Phase
**Tool:** axe DevTools Enterprise
**Target:** All 20 pages
**Acceptance:** All automated rules pass; no violations at CRITICAL/SERIOUS severity
**Process:**
1. Scan each page; export JSON results
2. Filter out known third-party findings (reCAPTCHA, YouTube)
3. Group findings by WCAG criterion
4. Assign each to remediation team with WCAG citation + specific element reference

### Manual Keyboard Testing Phase
**Tool:** Playwright + CDP
**Target:** Group C (6 auth pages) + Group D (8 shared components)
**Acceptance:** All keyboard interactions pass per APG patterns
**Test cases per interactive element:**
```
Example: Disclosure Toggle
- Tab focuses the button
- Space toggles aria-expanded true → false
- Space toggles aria-expanded false → true
- Panel shown when aria-expanded="true"
- Panel hidden when aria-expanded="false"
- Escape key has no effect (not a modal)
- Screen reader announces "expanded" or "collapsed" on toggle
```

### Screen Reader Testing Phase
**Tool:** Real SR (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) + Codified checks
**Target:** Group C + Group B sample
**Acceptance:** Structure, labels, state, and dynamic content announced correctly
**Test matrix (per page):**
1. Launch page, enter SR browse mode
2. Navigate by landmarks (n key in NVDA)
3. Navigate by headings (h key)
4. Verify heading hierarchy (no skips, appropriate levels)
5. Verify links have descriptive text (Tab through all links, verify announcement)
6. On forms: Tab to each input, verify label announced
7. Trigger form validation, verify error message announced and associated with field
8. Trigger dynamic updates, verify live region announces change

### Visual Regression Phase
**Tool:** Playwright screenshots + manual contrast analysis
**Target:** All sample pages
**Acceptance:** Focus indicators visible, contrast ratios met, zoom reflow successful
**Specific checks:**
- **Contrast:** Use axe's contrast rules to verify; spot-check interactive element focus rings
- **200% zoom:** Render each page at 200% viewport; verify horizontal scroll not needed; all elements readable
- **400% zoom:** At 320px equivalent viewport (WCAG 1.4.10); horizontal scroll acceptable; core content reachable
- **High-contrast mode:** Enable Windows High Contrast; rerender; verify focus indicators and interactive elements still distinguishable
- **Focus indicator:** Tab through page; verify outline visible, not obscured; 2-color ring recommended (outline + box-shadow)

---

## Implementation Tasks & a11y-Critic Checkpoints

### Task 1: Baseline Automated Audit
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineer 1

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** Baseline findings documented, duplicates and third-party findings filtered, critical findings identified

**Process:**
1. Install axe DevTools Enterprise browser extension
2. Configure ruleset: WCAG 2.2 AA, exclude reCAPTCHA/YouTube iframes
3. Open each page in DevTools; run Full Page Scan
4. Export JSON report
5. Group findings by WCAG criterion
6. Identify CRITICAL issues: form labels missing, focus order wrong, no alt text
7. Produce summary: Total violations, high/medium/low breakdown, estimated effort

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All 20 pages scanned
- Violations mapped to WCAG criteria
- Third-party findings documented separately
- Prioritized list of top 10 findings ready for remediation team

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Do automated findings align with WCAG 2.2 AA criteria? Are false positives filtered? Is third-party scope correctly excluded?

---

### Task 2: Shared Component Audit
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineer 2

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** All 8 shared components mapped to APG patterns, structure stubs verified, ARIA attributes specified

**Process:**
1. Identify shared component instances across pages (nav menu, search, alerts, table, file upload, date picker, modal, validation)
2. Extract component HTML and review current structure
3. For each component, document current ARIA implementation
4. Map to APG pattern with citation (e.g., https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/)
5. Identify missing/incorrect ARIA attributes
6. List keyboard interactions required (Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys, Escape)
7. Document state communication (aria-expanded, aria-pressed, aria-invalid, etc.)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All 8 components documented
- Each mapped to APG pattern with URL
- Current ARIA attributes listed with gaps identified
- Keyboard interactions specified per APG
- Structure stubs created (no implementation code; semantic elements + ARIA attributes only)

**Example for Mega-Menu Navigation:**
```
Component: Global Navigation Mega-Menu
APG Pattern: Menu Button (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubutton/)

Current Structure:
<nav>
  <button>Menu</button>  <!-- missing aria-expanded, aria-haspopup -->
  <ul style="display: none">  <!-- should use hidden attribute or aria-hidden -->
    <li><a href="/home">Home</a></li>
    ...
  </ul>
</nav>

Required ARIA:
- button: aria-expanded (true/false) — WCAG 4.1.2
- button: aria-haspopup="menu" — WCAG 4.1.2
- ul: role="menu" — WCAG 1.3.1
- li: role="none" — WCAG 1.3.1
- a (inside menu): role="menuitem" — WCAG 1.3.1

Keyboard Interactions:
- Tab to button
- Space/Enter: toggle aria-expanded
- Arrow Down: focus first menu item
- Arrow Down/Up: navigate menu items
- Escape: close menu, restore focus to button

Focus Management:
- On open: focus first menu item
- On close (Escape or click away): focus button
- Tab within menu wraps from last to first item (roving tabindex)
```

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Does each component map to a real APG pattern? Are all required ARIA attributes specified with WCAG citations? Is keyboard interaction model complete? Focus management planned?

---

### Task 3: Authenticated Flow Audit
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineers 1 + 2 (parallel)

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** All 6 auth pages tested, focus management verified, form interaction audited, WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.1 findings documented

**Pages tested:** Login, Account Creation, Multi-step Form (6 steps), Document Upload, Status Dashboard, Notification Center

**Process:**
1. **Keyboard Testing:**
   - Tab through each page; document tab order
   - Verify order matches visual left-to-right, top-to-bottom
   - Test form activation: Tab to button, Enter activates
   - Test modal (session timeout): Tab cycles within modal, Escape closes
   - Test Shift+Tab (reverse navigation)
   - Test arrow keys in date picker (if present)
   - Document any keyboard traps

2. **Focus Management:**
   - On page load, initial focus (skip link or first interactive element)
   - On modal open, focus moves to modal
   - On modal close, focus returns to trigger button
   - On form error, error message announced; focus stays in field or moves to error summary (document approach)
   - After form submission (success or error), focus restoration clear

3. **Screen Reader Testing (NVDA + VoiceOver):**
   - Page landmarks announced (nav, main, footer)
   - h1 present, heading hierarchy correct
   - Form labels associated; announced on Tab
   - Form errors: aria-invalid="true" on field, error message linked via aria-describedby
   - Dynamic content: status updates announced via aria-live="polite"
   - Session timeout modal: trap focus, announce danger, Escape restores focus

4. **Form-Specific Checks:**
   - Every input has label (visible + programmatic)
   - Error messages specific (not "Invalid input"; use "Email missing @ symbol")
   - Required fields marked (visually + aria-required="true")
   - Multi-step form: current step announced (aria-current="step" or role="status")
   - Submit button name clear (e.g., "Continue to Next" not just "Next")

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All 6 pages tested with keyboard; issues logged
- Focus restoration verified on all overlays/modals
- Form labels audited; aria-invalid + aria-describedby documented
- Screen reader test notes captured (per SR, per page)
- CRITICAL issues (keyboard trap, no labels, focus lost) flagged for immediate remediation

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Are focus management flows correct? Do all form fields have labels and error associations? Is keyboard navigation complete (no traps)? Do modals trap focus and restore properly?

---

### Task 4: Content & Landing Page Audit
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineer 2

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** Alt text audit complete, link text quality verified, video captions confirmed, contrast & zoom tested

**Pages tested:** Home, Contact, Program Listings, Program Detail (1 variant), FAQ, News

**Specific checks:**

**Alt Text Audit (WCAG 1.1.1):**
- Decorative images: alt="" present
- Informative images: concise alt text (e.g., "Graph of unemployment trends 2020-2024")
- Complex images (infographics): short alt + `aria-describedby` link to long description

**Link Text (WCAG 2.4.4):**
- All links have descriptive text (not "click here", "read more", "learn more")
- New window links marked "(opens in new window)"
- Review context: link in prose vs. link in navigation (nav links exempt from underline requirement per WCAG 1.4.1)

**Form on Contact Page (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.2):**
- All inputs labeled via `<label for="">`
- reCAPTCHA has clear instructions (keyboard user can complete?)
- Submit button name clear ("Send Message")
- Error message specific + linked to field via aria-describedby

**Video Embeds (WCAG 1.2.1, 1.2.2):**
- YouTube videos: captions enabled (cc icon visible in player)
- Captions are accurate (spot-check 1-2 videos)
- Transcript available or linked (if captions insufficient)

**Heading Hierarchy (WCAG 1.3.1):**
- h1 present, unique per page
- h2-h6 no skips (h2 → h3 → h4 not h2 → h4)
- Headings describe content (not "Section 1", "Content", etc.)

**Visual Tests (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.10, 2.4.7):**
- Screenshot each page at 200% zoom; verify no horizontal scroll
- Spot-check contrast: text on background 4.5:1 (normal), 3:1 (large 18px+)
- Focus indicator visible on all interactive elements

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Alt text audit spreadsheet: [image ID, current alt, issue?, suggested fix]
- Link text issues logged by page
- Form fields verified labeled + error handling clear
- Video captions confirmed
- Heading hierarchy documented (h1, h2, h3, etc. per page outline)
- Zoom/contrast screenshots taken

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Is alt text meaningful and appropriate (decorative vs. informative)? Are link texts descriptive? Do forms have proper labels and error communication? Are videos captioned? Does heading hierarchy reflect document structure?

---

### Task 5: Visual Accessibility Testing
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineer 1

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** Contrast ratios verified, focus indicators documented, responsive behavior at high zoom confirmed, color not sole indicator

**Process:**

**Contrast Verification (WCAG 1.4.3):**
1. Use axe's contrast rule as baseline
2. Manually spot-check interactive elements (buttons, links, focus indicators)
3. Verify:
   - Normal text: 4.5:1
   - Large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold): 3:1
   - Focus indicator (outline): contrasts with background
   - Disabled elements: no contrast requirement (disabled, not error state)

**Focus Indicator Testing (WCAG 2.4.7):**
1. Tab through each page
2. Screenshot focus indicator on key elements (button, input, link, tab)
3. Verify outline visible at:
   - 100% zoom (normal)
   - 200% zoom (magnified)
   - 400% zoom (high magnification)
   - High-contrast mode (Windows High Contrast toggle on)
4. Verify no focus obscured by dropdown/popover
5. Recommend 2-color focus ring: `outline` + `box-shadow` (e.g., dark outline + light box-shadow)

**Zoom & Reflow Testing (WCAG 1.4.10):**
1. Render page at 200% zoom; verify no horizontal scroll needed; all content readable
2. Render page at 400% zoom (viewport = 320px equivalent); horizontal scroll acceptable but content reachable
3. Verify touch targets at high zoom are still usable (44x44 minimum)

**Animation & Motion (WCAG 2.3.3):**
1. Check CSS for `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rules
2. Verify animations disabled when user preference set
3. Test on Windows (Settings > Ease of Access > Display > Show animations)

**Color Not Sole Indicator (WCAG 1.4.1):**
1. Audit every color-coded element:
   - Required field: red border → should also have `*` icon or text
   - Error field: red border + error message + aria-invalid="true"
   - Success: green checkmark → should also have text "Verified"
   - Disabled: gray button → should have disabled attribute, aria-disabled="true", or `[disabled]` class
2. Identify violations; document remediation

**High-Contrast Mode (WCAG 1.4.11):**
1. Enable Windows High Contrast mode (Settings > Ease of Access > Display > High Contrast)
2. Render sample pages
3. Verify interactive elements (buttons, links) still distinguishable
4. Verify focus indicators visible
5. If CSS uses hard-coded colors, verify they work in forced-colors mode (CSS `forced-color-adjust: none` may be needed)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Contrast verification spreadsheet: [element, foreground, background, ratio, pass/fail]
- Focus indicator screenshots at 100%, 200%, 400% zoom, high-contrast
- Reflow screenshots (200%, 400% zoom)
- Animation check: prefers-reduced-motion rules documented
- Color-coding audit: list of elements, non-color alternatives
- Recommendations for focus ring CSS

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Are contrast ratios sufficient? Are focus indicators visible and distinctive? Does page reflow at 400% zoom? Are animations disabled per prefers-reduced-motion? Is color never the sole indicator?

---

### Task 6: Remediation & Regression Testing
**Duration:** 2 weeks
**Owner:** Development Team (external); QA oversight

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** Fix commit logs reviewed, regression tests pass, fixed issues verified against audit findings

**Process:**
1. Dev team receives prioritized list of CRITICAL and MAJOR findings
2. For each finding, dev team:
   - Creates branch for fix
   - Modifies code per accessibility plan (e.g., adds aria-expanded, aria-describedby, focus trap logic)
   - Writes test (Playwright keyboard test, axe scan test)
   - Submits PR for QA review

3. QA Engineer reviews:
   - Code matches accessibility plan (correct ARIA attributes, focus management, state communication)
   - Tests pass (keyboard navigation, contrast, alt text)
   - No new violations introduced (re-run axe on fixed pages)
   - Fix addresses specific finding (e.g., focus now restores after modal close)

4. QA Engineer re-tests:
   - Tab through fixed page; verify focus restoration
   - Run axe scan; verify no new violations
   - Test with screen reader (spot-check key elements)
   - Take screenshot at 200% zoom; verify reflow still works

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All CRITICAL findings remediated and tested
- All MAJOR findings remediated (with clear timeline for lower-priority)
- No regression (new violations introduced)
- Regression test suite established (automated scans + manual spot-checks on every commit)

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Do fixes correctly implement the accessibility plan? Are keyboard interactions working as designed? Is focus management complete? Have regressions been introduced?

### Task 7: VPAT Compilation & Final Audit
**Duration:** 1 week
**Owner:** QA Engineer 1 + Legal/Compliance Review

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 document complete, criterion-by-criterion claims accurate, Appendix C (third-party notes) finalized, legal review passed

**Process:**

1. **Map Findings to WCAG Criteria:**
   - For each automated + manual finding, identify which WCAG criterion it violates
   - Tally conformance per criterion: Y (met), N (not met), N/A (not applicable)
   - Document specific examples (page, element, finding)

2. **Compile Criterion-by-Criterion Table:**
   ```
   | WCAG Criterion | Title | Level | Status | Notes |
   | 1.1.1 Non-text Content | Images have alt text | A | Y | ✓ All images alt-textured; checked 20 pages |
   | 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) | Video has captions | A | Y | ✓ All program videos captioned |
   | 1.3.1 Info and Relationships | Semantic structure | A | N | ✗ Form fields on login not labeled; 3 tables lack headers; mega-menu missing role="menu" |
   | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
   ```

3. **Write Appendix C (Explanatory Notes):**
   - **Audit Methodology:** Pages tested (12 of 20), sampling strategy, tools used (axe, Playwright, manual)
   - **WCAG-EM Reference:** W3C Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology 1.0 (or 2.0)
   - **Unmet Criteria Remediation Plan:** For each criterion marked "N", provide timeline (Week 1-2, Week 3-4, post-VPAT, etc.)
   - **Third-Party Components:**
     ```
     reCAPTCHA v2: Third-party (Google Inc.). Known issues: Confusing keyboard interaction, unclear error messaging for users with cognitive disabilities. Remediation: Planned upgrade to reCAPTCHA v3 or alternative solution by [date].
     
     YouTube Embedded Videos: Third-party (Google Inc.). Accessibility depends on caption availability in source video. All program videos are required to have captions per Section 508 compliance. Player is keyboard-accessible; captions are user-controlled.
     
     Google Analytics: No accessibility implications.
     ```

4. **Conformance Statement:**
   - Template: "[Portal Name] is committed to being accessible to all users. This Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) documents conformance to WCAG 2.2 Level AA per W3C evaluation methodology. As of [date], [Portal] conforms to X of 50 Level A/AA criteria. Identified gaps are listed in Appendix C with remediation timeline. For questions, contact [Accessibility Email]."

5. **Legal Review:**
   - Compliance team reviews VPAT
   - Verify criterion claims are accurate (no overclaiming)
   - Confirm third-party disclosures are legally sound
   - Approve for publication

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 document complete per ITTF template
- Criterion-by-criterion claims (Y/N/N/A) justified with evidence
- Appendix C addresses all unmet criteria + third-party components + remediation plan
- Legal review sign-off
- Document ready for publication

**a11y-critic checkpoint:** Are criterion claims accurate? Is evidence provided (page, element, finding)? Are remediation plans realistic? Are third-party exceptions correctly documented? Is conformance statement appropriate?

### Task 8: Monitoring & Maintenance (Post-VPAT)
**Duration:** Ongoing
**Owner:** QA Engineer + Dev Team

🔍 **Review checkpoint:** Regression test suite established, accessibility checks integrated into CI, new features tested before release

**Process:**
1. **Automated Regression Testing:**
   - Add axe scans to CI pipeline (on every commit)
   - Create Playwright keyboard tests for fixed components (Tab order, focus restoration, modal traps)
   - Set up visual regression (screenshot comparison on key pages)

2. **New Feature Accessibility Checklist:**
   - Before any new feature ships: QA runs axe scan, keyboard test, screen reader spot-check
   - Accessibility plan required for interactive components (use a11y-planner)
   - Fixes must include tests + WCAG citations

3. **Quarterly Audit Updates:**
   - Re-run full site scan (axe) quarterly to detect new issues
   - Re-test shared components quarterly to verify no regression
   - Update VPAT if new unmet criteria discovered

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Automated test suite in CI
- New features accessibility pre-flight checklist in place
- Quarterly audit schedule documented
- Accessibility POC identified for ongoing ownership

## Risk Mitigation

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Large site, small team, tight deadline | Risk-based page sampling (focus on auth flows, shared components). Shared component fixes multiply value. Estimate 8-10 weeks realistically; escalate if remediation slower than expected. |
| Unknown baseline accessibility state | Week 1 automated scan provides rapid baseline. If >500 violations found, prioritize top 20 CRITICAL issues; patch iteratively. |
| Third-party components block conformance claims | Document in VPAT Appendix C upfront. Do not overclaim. Plan upgrade path (reCAPTCHA v3, etc.). Legal review before publication. |
| Screen reader testing requires real SR + user skill | Use Playwright + NVDA (free, open-source) first; JAWS/VoiceOver later if budget allows. Codify keyboard tests (automated); SR tests (manual spot-checks). |
| Focus management is hardest to automate | Require manual Playwright tests for every interactive pattern. No "figure it out later." Tests must verify Tab order, focus trap, focus restoration. |
| Keyboard traps block keyboard users | Audit every composite widget (modal, menu, tab panel). Require roving tabindex or ARIA-active-descendant. Tab should always work or trap should be intentional + documented. |
| Remediation takes longer than 2 weeks | Parallel fixes: QA testing Group C while Dev remediates Group D findings; stagger by 1 week. |

## Conclusion

This comprehensive audit plan provides a risk-based, WCAG-EM-grounded strategy for systematically evaluating a 20-page government portal within a 3-month VPAT deadline. By leveraging automated tools for breadth (all 20 pages), manual testing for depth (12 priority pages), and shared-component leverage (8 patterns fixing all pages), a 2-person QA team can establish a complete accessibility baseline, prioritize remediation, and produce a legally sound VPAT document. Success depends on early prioritization, clear tools and processes, parallel testing phases, and realistic remediation expectations.
